title: HostedAPI ephemeral-heartbeat oscillation playbook (draft)
body:
Summary:
We saw a P0-level surge in streaming session instability concentrated at midnight UTC in eu-west-1. Symptom: sustained p95/p99 TTFB and streaming chunk fragmentation for ~18 minutes, with ~23% session resets and 12% spike in 5xx responses for streaming endpoints. User-facing: realtime chat and long-running inference streams experienced partial responses and reconnects.

High-level hypothesis (root cause):
A confluence of three factors:
1) a client-side ramp of aggressive ephemeral heartbeat (shorter-than-usual keepalive) from a large partner testing an SDK change, causing many connections to rapidly reassert and re-register streams;
2) a concurrent TLS ticket rotation job (edge-TLS) that caused a subset of edge nodes to fail session resumption, forcing new TLS handshakes which significantly increased CPU and acceptor thread time;
3) the acceptor pool on a fraction of frontends has a work-queue sizing bug that degrades when burst concurrency crosses a threshold -> long acceptor lock hold + poll throttling -> streaming write stalls and partial chunk flushes.

Impact and scope:
- Duration: 2029-04-11 00:07 UTC -> 2029-04-11 00:25 UTC (18m)
- Affected region: eu-west-1 edge cluster primarily, small spill to us-west due to routing fallback
- Customer-visible: 2.1% of all streaming requests returned 5xx, 23% of active streaming sessions experienced reconnects; non-stream (sync) endpoints had <0.5% increase in errors
- Severity: P0 (service degradation on hosted streaming endpoints)

Detection timeline (short):
- 00:07 UTC: synthetic monitors (p95 streaming TTFB) alert
- 00:08 UTC: on-call acknowledges, pulls SLO dashboard (console) -> sees p99 jump
- 00:09 UTC: SRE triage Slack channel populated; initial suspects: autoscaler/throttling
- 00:12 UTC: edge telemetry shows TLS ticket rotation events correlated with acceptor CPU spikes on node subset
- 00:14 UTC: partner engineering confirms they deployed SDK test that reduced keepalive to 5s on a canary cohort (recent change)
- 00:18 UTC: mitigation applied (edge TLS rotation coordinated rollback + temporarily increase acceptor queue size and enable backpressure bypass on affected frontends)
- 00:25 UTC: metrics recovering; alerts resolved by 00:36 UTC after gradual cool-down and routing adjustments

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Coordinated with edge ops to pause TLS ticket rotation job on eu-west-1 (rollback of scheduled rotation) -> reduced full-handshake volume
- Temp increase of acceptor queue limit on affected frontend fleet (kernel tunables & process env) to avoid immediate queue overflow
- Activated streaming fallback policy: route new streams to dedicated streaming-capable frontends (lower burst susceptibility)
- Throttled partner SDK cohort via WAF rule to reduce heartbeat frequency while partner rolled back their change

Why these mitigations helped:
- Preventing TLS rotation allowed session resumption to remain effective for most clients, removing the sudden CPU/handshake load
- Increasing queue limits bought time for frontend workers to catch up without dropping streams
- Routing away streams from the susceptible fleet avoided further amplification while we diagnosed

Root cause analysis (deeper):
- The acceptor queue sizing code path (acceptor_pool::enqueue) incorrectly computes available slots under high accept-rate when keepalive churn creates many short-lived streams. The bug manifests when enqueue_rate > dequeue_rate for >30s and a specific heap-balancer path engages -> leads to a mutex backoff loop and delayed poll wakeups.
- Edge TLS rotation introduced concurrent new-handshake traffic by invalidating session tickets; this turned what would have been cheap resumptions into expensive full handshakes on already-burdened nodes.
- Client-side change: partner SDK reduced keepalive/heartbeat interval from 30s->5s in a canary release; amplification factor was ~6x active reconnections. They did not include jitter which caused synchronized reconnection bursts.

Contributing factors (systemic):
- Missing safeguard: acceptor queue had no fast-failback for sustained enqueue pressure (we relied on autoscaler to handle capacity but autoscaler reacts slower than the burst)
- Monitoring gap: we had good global metrics but lacked a high-resolution acceptor lock contention metric and a cross-correlation alert tying TLS rotation events to acceptor CPU directly (we inferred via logs)
- Partner coordination: SDK change lacked a staged jitter policy and an appropriate rollout key for high-cardinality customers

Runbook draft (proposed steps to use if similar pattern detected):
1) Immediately identify if TLS ticket rotation is active in the region (edge-ops TL) -> if yes, pause/rollback rotation for region
2) Query acceptor-queue-length and lock-wait-time metrics; if queue_length > threshold && lock_wait > X ms -> increase acceptor queue limits on a small subset of nodes and re-route streaming traffic
3) Apply WAF throttling rule to suspected client cohort (quick mitigation while partner rolls back)
4) If fragmentation seen (partial-chunk flushes), activate streaming fallback route to dedicated frontends and temporarily extend stream idle timeouts to avoid premature resets
5) Post-incident: capture heap-profiles, acceptor contention traces, and TLS handshake logs for 5m before and after mitigation actions

Automated playbook knobs (operators):
- edge.tls.rotation.pause <region> (operator playbook)
- frontend.acceptor.queue.set <fleet> <value> (Respawnless env toggle)
- routing.stream.route-to <backend-tag> (traffic-split)
- waf.client.heartbeat-throttle <client-id> <rate> (quick block/ratelimit)

Longer-term fixes and owners:
- engineering/serving-runtime: patch acceptor_pool::enqueue to add fast-path when dequeue lag detected + add unit/bench tests (owner: Diego Ramos, ETA: 3w)
- edge-team: add safe-rotation mode that staggers ticket rotation across edge slices and exposes telemetry (owner: Samir Patel, ETA: 2w)
- observability: add acceptor-lock-wait and handshake-failure coalert; add dashboard linking TLS rotation to acceptor CPU (owner: Olivia Chen, ETA: 1w)
- partner-eng: update SDK best-practices doc to require jittered backoff and staged rollout keys for heartbeat changes; push a client-side guard to prevent sub-10s keepalive without explicit opt-in (owner: Partner Eng contact / Maya Singh, ETA: 1w)
- ops: create a canned incident runbook (this doc) and test playbook in chaos exercise next sprint (owner: eng-sre, ETA: next chaos week)

Action items (short):
- [Ava] Create PR with patch to acceptor queue logic + perf test harness (PR target: in 48h)
- [Diego] Run bench to reproduce enqueue/dequeue divergence locally and capture trace (48h)
- [Samir] Implement staggered rotation plan and run safe-rotation on eu-west-1 (1w)
- [Olivia] Add coalert and dashboard tiles; create alert runbooks (72h)
- [Maya] Coordinate partner rollback verification and update SDK guidance (immediate)

Postmortem notes and open questions:
- Need to decide if acceptor queue default should be raised globally or if we prefer proactive traffic shaping early (tradeoff: memory & latency).
- Confirm whether other partners with large connection counts have client-side fast reconnects enabled; run a sweep of high-cardinality customers for 7d of reconnection spikes.
- Capture a small sample of full-handshake TLS CPU profiles for future simulation.

Oncall playbook checklist (quick):
- check region TLS rotation status (edge ops console)
- query acceptor_queue_length (last 5m) and lock_wait_ms
- if lock_wait_ms > 200ms -> increase acceptor queue for 20% fleet and route new streams elsewhere
- if handshake_rate > baseline*3 -> pause TLS rotation and deploy safe-rotation
- if client cohort identified -> apply temporary WAF throttle and notify partner

Notes to future responders:
- Prioritize stopping the expensive source (handshakes / synchronized reconnects) over dropping sessions. Avoid broad connection kill except as last resort.
- Keep communication tight with partner eng when SDK changes are suspected; require immediate rollback if they cannot show jittered rollout.

Appendix: useful queries and commands (for runbook)
- metrics query: sum(rate(edge_tls.handshakes[1m])) by (node)
- metrics query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(frontend.acceptor.lock_wait_bucket[1m])) by (le, node))
- logs: tail -f logs/edge/handshake-*.log | grep "ticket rotate"
- temp WAF command: waf-cli apply --rule heartbeat-throttle --client <id> --rate 1/s --duration 30m

End of draft. Please add any additional hypotheses, test results, or commands you used during incident response.
